# Page 1^page=1
Data bases 2 Reliability Control

# Page 2^page=2
Reliability For which transaction properties? • Atomicity: all or nothing semantics • Durability: persistence of effect With which basic mechanisms? • Stable memory  Backup • Log for recovery

# Page 3^page=3
Backup mechanims 3 • Example in MySQL Dimension Main Options Notes Backup form Physical / Logical File copy vs. SQL export Server state Online (hot) / Offline (cold) Live vs. stopped Location Local / Remote On-host or over network Technique Snapshot / Full / Incremental At specific time points/ Entire copy/ Only changes since last backup Recovery Full / Point-in-time Log replay full or up to timestamp Other functiontalities Scheduling / Compression / Encryption Usually external or enterprise tools https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/backup-types.html

# Page 4^page=4
Buffer Management Policies When to write modified (“dirty”) pages back to disk? 4 Policy Description Pros Cons FORCE When a transaction commits, all its modified pages are forced to disk immediately. Simpler recovery (no REDO needed). Slower commits → must wait for disk I/O. NO- FORCE Committed changes may stay in memory; writing to disk is delayed until later (e.g., during checkpoint or buffer replacement). Faster commits (asynchronous I/O). Needs REDO during recovery, since committed data may still be only in RAM.

# Page 5^page=5
Buffer Management Policies Policy Description Pros Cons STEAL The buffer manager may “steal” a dirty page even if the transaction that modified it hasn’t committed yet Reduces memory pressure (frees buffer space) Requires UNDO during recovery, because uncommitted changes might reach disk NO-STEAL Dirty pages of uncommitted transactions cannot be evicted — they stay in memory until commit or rollback Simplifies recovery (no UNDO needed) May block new transactions if memory is full Which dirty pages can be “evicted” and written into the secondary memory?

# Page 6^page=6
Example T1: Not committed but stolen pages! T2: Committed but dirty pages have not been written!! T3: Committed and written onto disk T4: Not committed but everything only in main memory

# Page 11^page=11
Periodically: checkpoint  T2 and T3 already ended  They must be written to secondary storage (committed and permanently stored)  T1 and T4 are in progress  List in the checkpoint active transactions  CKPT(T1,T4) Active: T1, T4 Finished: T2, T3 In MySQL: fuzzy checkpointing  The system gradually writes dirty pages to disk while transactions continue running.
